biocom-satomic-ai:rippling:deb151d2-d9e7.description: About Satomic Satomic’s mission is to close the gap from idea to molecule with faster navigation of chemical space. We are building an automated chemistry platform that integrates laboratory robotics, software, and AI to transform small-molecule synthesis and drug discovery. Satomic has raised a $15M Seed from fantastic investors including Riot Ventures, HOF Capital, and Compound VC, and our team includes alumni from leading large pharmas, small biotechs, and AI labs. This role is critical to Satomic’s mission of closing the gap from idea to molecule by building the chemistry search engine that lets our customers see, query, and reach into Satomic’s accessible chemical space: trillions of multistep-accessible molecules grounded in the platform’s actual synthesis capabilities. You will take in constraints from our automation team, conversion and substrate-scope models from our ML team, and building blocks from our vendors to define the complete specification of Satomic's accessible chemical space. This role is a founding-engineer position within the Development team. You'll be the technical owner of the cheminformatics domain — defining its standards and its architecture — while working as part of a broader engineering group that owns the platform you're building on. You will partner closely with our data science / ML lead and work day-to-day with the rest of Development on the systems your engine integrates with. You will have exposure to end users at Satomic’s commercial partners to translate user behavior into the query types the engine should support. We believe being part of the chemistry-AI conversation externally (through publication, open source, and the conferences and forums where this field develops) is part of the job. This is a hands-on role for an engineer who thrives with extreme latitude, ownership, and judgment. You will decide what to build versus buy on cheminformatics-specific tooling (RDKit / OpenEye for chemistry primitives, AiZynthFinder / ASKCOS / Synthia / IBM RXN for retrosynthesis, pharmacophore tooling, IP / FTO filtering, vector index choice), choose the engine's core representations, and define the versioning rules that keep it correct as chemistry capabilities expand.Infrastructure-adjacent choices — vector index, storage layer, serving framework — are made jointly with the team. gaingels-atomic-industries:ashbyhq:a3c78.description: Job Title: Quality Technician – Injection Molding Location: Shelby Township, MI Company: Atomic Industries Reports To: Quality Manager ABOUT ATOMIC INDUSTRIES Atomic Industries is reinventing how the world makes things. From cars and aerospace systems to medical devices and packaging, most physical goods begin life in a mold or are shaped by a manufacturing tool. Producing these tools has always been slow, manual, and dependent on scarce expertise, taking weeks or months. We’re changing that. At our Detroit headquarters, we combine the industrial DNA of America’s manufacturing heartland with the speed, intelligence, and precision of Silicon Valley. Our AI-driven platform tackles the hardest problems in geometry, process planning, and fabrication, collapsing production timelines from months to days and soon, minutes. We don’t just build software; we run a fully operational factory where our technology produces production-grade tooling every week, enabling tight feedback loops and rapid iteration. Backed by top-tier investors, we’re restoring speed, flexibility, and capability to the American industrial base. Our mission is to make manufacturing as agile and scalable as the digital world, and in doing so, rebuild the infrastructure of the physical economy. POSITION OVERVIEW We’re seeking a detail-oriented and dependable Quality Technician to support quality control and inspection across our injection molding operations. You’ll be on the floor inspecting parts, maintaining records, and working closely with process engineers and toolmakers to ensure every part meets Atomic’s exacting standards. This is a key hands-on role as we scale high-volume production and build out our ISO-compliant quality systems. gaingels-included-health:lever:1d4ee2b9-.title: Medical Director of Clinical Affairs
gaingels-included-health:lever:1d4ee2b9-.description: About Included Health Included Health is a new kind of healthcare company, delivering integrated virtual care and navigation to millions of members throughout the country. We’re on a mission to raise the standard of healthcare for everyone. We break down barriers to provide high-quality care for every person in every community no matter where they are in their health journey or what type of care they need—from acute to chronic, behavioral to physical. We offer our members care guidance, advocacy, and access to personalized virtual and in-person care for everyday and urgent care, primary care, behavioral health, and specialty care. It’s all included. Learn more at includedhealth.com. Position Overview The Medical Director - Clinical Affairs serves as a vital strategic clinical partner bridging Included Health, our strategic clients, and external stakeholders. This role is designed for a visionary physician-leader who can think of new and creative ways—leveraging data and technology—to improve the healthcare experience in a way that promotes better clinical and financial outcomes. The ideal candidate will not only represent the value of Included Health’s clinical offerings to support growth and retention but will also act as an executive-level clinical advisor to our most complex clients. They will translate population health data into actionable clinical campaigns, clinically steer multi-vendor ecosystems (including TPAs and carriers), and collaborate with internal business strategy teams to scale repeatable clinical solutions in the market.
responsibilities: Pillar 1: Clinical Stewardship & Support for Strategic Clients

Executive Advisory: Serve as a trusted clinical thought leader for strategic enterprise clients, advising executive committees on topics such as clinical policy guardrails, healthcare AI integration, and benefits strategy.

Population Health Strategy & Analytics: Analyze population utilization data to develop strategies, rising-risk briefs, and clinical campaign designs that alter the cost and health trajectory of client populations.
High-Stakes Case Support: Manage the high-stakes, high-visibility, or high-dollar case desk—providing clinical case memos, peer-to-peer discussions, and member-facing clinical framing guidance.

Population Health Informatics & Efficiency: Review aggregate member health and claims data to uncover systemic inefficiencies and low-value care patterns, providing plan sponsors with clinical guidance on how to optimize their benefit ecosystem.

Joint Vendor Stewardship: Lead multi-vendor clinical rounds bringing together Included Health, client HR leaders, third-party administrators (TPAs), carriers, and other point-solutions to align on clinical action plans.

Clinically Led HCC Management: Direct the clinical narrative around High Cost Claimants (HCC) within client populations, moving HCC efforts from static reporting to active, clinically led member support.
Pillar 2: Growth Strategy & Support for Sales and External Partners

Sales & Retention Enablement: Partner with Sales and Client Success teams during high-stakes prospect pitches and renewal cycles to showcase the clinical and economic value of our programs, driving upsells, revenue generation, and customer retention.
External Representation: Represent Included Health at national conferences, industry events, and seminars to showcase our clinical performance, navigation, and virtual care capabilities.
Educational Engagement: Develop and deliver highly engaging educational materials and clinical presentations for clients, healthcare professionals, and public stakeholders.
Pillar 3: Internal Support & Business Strategy

Scalable Clinical Strategy: Partner directly with the Business Strategy team to evaluate external vendors, co-develop our clinical strategy, identify emerging market needs, and determine what clinical offerings can be delivered effectively at scale.

Health Plan Strategy & Market Integration: Leverage health plan and TPA expertise to build out consistent, structured clinical support for the health plan side of our business, assisting with ecosystem integration, strategic carrier collaborations, and the expansion of innovative models like Alternative Plan Design (APD).
qualifications: Professional Background / Requirements
Education: Medical Doctor (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) degree.

Clinical Experience: Minimum of 5 years of post-residency clinical experience. High-quality clinical baseline across a wide range of medical conditions is highly preferred to support high-stakes case navigation.
Licensure: Active medical license in good standing in state of residence. Must maintain board certification in primary specialty throughout employment.
Travel: Willingness to travel up to twice per month for 1-2 days each (averaged over the year) for client engagements and conferences, occasionally with short notice.
Specialized Expertise (Highly Preferred)

Clinical Consulting & Strategy: Proven experience in clinical consulting through experience such as corporate/health plan Medical Director, clinical SME in the digital health field, or through work in healthcare consulting.
Health Plan & TPA Acumen: Deep working knowledge of Health Plans, TPAs, and commercial benefit ecosystems, with direct experience in Alternative Plan Design (APD) or health plan client support.

Population Health and Claims Acumen: Experience analyzing healthcare claims, utilization reports, or clinical data to pull out population trends, track clinical quality, and identify opportunities to improve healthcare spend.
Digital Health Expertise: Comprehensive understanding of the digital health landscape, emerging clinical technology trends (including AI in care), and virtual care delivery models.

gaingels-lynk:ashbyhq:cde26cc6-c647-4cc1.title: RF Systems Test Engineer
gaingels-lynk:ashbyhq:cde26cc6-c647-4cc1.description: About Lynk Lynk is the inventor of satellite direct to standard phone technology aka sat2phone, and has the world’s only commercial license from the FCC to operate a commercial sat2phone system. Today, Lynk allows mobile network operators' subscribers to send and receive text messages to and from space via standard unmodified, mobile devices. Lynk’s service has been tested and proven on all seven continents, has regulatory approvals in more than 30 countries and is currently being deployed commercially based on more than 40 MNO commercial service contracts covering approximately 50 countries. Our technology will enable all 8 billion people on the planet to stay connected with the existing standard phone in their pocket. Everywhere. No matter what. By joining Lynk, you will have the opportunity to directly touch the lives of billions. Your mission will be to bring mobile broadband to billions, pull hundreds of millions out of poverty, and save countless lives. Job Summary As a RF Systems Test Engineer at Lynk, you will wear many hats in the world of RF hardware/electronics and software/firmware. The immediate role of the RF Systems Test Engineer will be to support testing of the company’s digital phased array antenna payload hardware in the lab environment. While playing with all this hardware on a bench, you will probably need to pick up a soldering gun, assemble circuits on a breadboard, use an oscilloscope, vector network analyzer, and spectrum analyzer. This role is critical to the success of our mission, as you will be at the center of developing and executing the automated testing and verification for every aspect of the digital phased array payload that makes our service possible. As an RF Systems Test Engineer you will be expected to understand every detail of this complex system design and its expected function, including high speed mixed signal beamformer boards, clock distribution networks, RFFE boards, integrated radiating antenna elements, and full array calibration and verification procedures. Core Responsibilities - Integrate flight and lab RF hardware electronics, design test beds, fixtures, etc. for operational verification of RF hardware and software technologies. - Design, develop, and document test and integration procedures for flight and lab RF hardware, particularly RF Front Ends, and Mixed-Signal Digital Electronics. - Design, develop, specify, and maintain hardware and software for Electronic Ground Support Equipment aka EGSE to be used to support satellite RF digital phased array payload verification, particularly before, during, and after functional and environmental testing. - Bench-level work with electronics to debug and troubleshoot issues that arise during testing, including functional and environmental testing. - Working alongside engineers and technicians, Inform the design, development, and optimization of the company’s operational testing procedures and policies for our Production and research and development campaign for our space technology. - Huge focus on automation for testing and data collection tools to ensure testing can be done reliably, repeatedly, and at scale in production. Basic Qualifications - A Bachelor’s degree or better in Electrical Engineering, RF Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or similar degrees. - 5+ years of experience as an RF Engineer focused on system design and/or test. - Experience with standard RF lab equipment is required: Oscilloscopes, Spectrum and Vector Network Analyzer, Multimeter, etc. - Hands-on experience with RFFE printed circuit boards, single-board computers, microcontrollers, FPGAs, GPUs, CPUs, SoCs, software-defined radios, and/or antennas. - Ability to read and understand datasheets for integrated circuits and electronics. - Experience using Linux based systems and programming proficiency in one or more programming languages, such as Rust, C++, C, Python, MATLAB, etc. - Must have good communicatio

southparkcommons-preference-models:ashby.description: ABOUT US Preference Model is building automated ML research engineering. Existing frontier models are brittle when applied to real-world ML tasks. The present bottleneck is the lack of high-quality RL training environments. Our first step is to build RL environments that reflect real-world complexity, with diverse tasks and robust reward functions. Our founding team has previous experience on Anthropic’s data team building data infrastructure, and datasets behind Claude. We are partnering with leading AI labs to push AI closer to achieving its transformative potential. ABOUT THE ROLE As part of our goal to automate every role at a hypothetical AI research lab. One important capability we care about is models' understanding of cybersecurity. We're hiring experienced Security / Cybersecurity Engineers to design and build reinforcement learning environments that teach LLMs to reason about and solve real-world cybersecurity problems, such as finding vulnerabilities in production codebases to generating working exploits and patching them safely. You'll join a small, high-ownership team and contribute directly to the data layer that powers frontier LLM capability in security. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Design and build RL environments and reward functions that produce clean, learnable signals for frontier models on offensive and defensive security tasks across diverse programming languages. - Build environments covering the full vulnerability lifecycle: discovery in source code, exploiting, patching. - Build environments for reverse engineering tasks across binaries, bytecode, and obfuscated code. - Construct verifiable reward signals using fuzzers, sanitizers, symbolic execution, static analyzers, exploit-success checks, and patch-correctness validation. - Collaborate with others to brainstorm and create new ideas and tools to improve the environment building process. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR - Strong security fundamentals and broad interests across both offensive and defensive work. You read advisories, papers, and writeups, understand vulnerabilities deeply, and have the creativity to translate them into RLVR problems. - Hands-on experience finding, exploiting, or patching real vulnerabilities through CTFs, bug bounty work, security research, red/blue team engagements, or shipped security work in industry. - Proficiency in Python and systems programming, plus working comfort in at least one low-level language (C, C++, Rust) and one web/application stack. - Familiarity with security tooling: fuzzers, sanitizers, debuggers, and disassemblers - Problem solvers who take ownership and drive solutions end-to-end. - Passion for staying current with the rapidly evolving security and ML landscape. - Ability to meet throughput expectations and respond quickly to feedback. NICE TO HAVE: - Published security research, CVEs, or notable bug bounty findings. - Strong CTF background or competitive results at events like DEF CON CTF, or similar. - Deep expertise in a specific area: binary exploitation, kernel security, browser/V8 internals, hypervisor security, cryptographic implementation, web application security, or cloud/container security. - Experience building or contributing to fuzzing infrastructure, vulnerability scanners, or automated program analysis tools. - Experience with ML for code or security. - You have built complex interactive RL environments, agent harnesses, or sandboxed evaluation infrastructure. WHAT WE OFFER: - Competitive cash and equity compensation (>90th percentile) - Ownership and autonomy in a fast moving startup environment - Opportunity to work with top machine learning engineers - Health, vision, dental, benefits - 401K match - Lunch provided everyday onsite - Weekly snack orders - Visa sponsorship & relocation support available We value diverse perspectives and experiences. If you're excited about this role but don't check every box, we still encourage you to apply.
